description:
Compare the Elixir TUI implementation (bin/pi) with the Node.js reference (pi-coding-agent) side-by-side to identify UI/UX differences in the /tree command and create parity tickets.

## Background
The /tree command in Node.js shows a rich overlay with:
- "Session Tree" header title
- Navigation hints (↑/↓: move, ←/→: page, etc.)
- "Type to search:" filter input
- Tree entries with selection marker (›)
- Entry count badge (e.g., "(2/3)")

The Elixir implementation currently only shows the tree entries without these UI elements.

## Sub-tickets
- opi-ce3.1: Add "Session Tree" header title
- opi-ce3.2: Add navigation hints row
- opi-ce3.3: Add search/filter input field
- opi-ce3.4: Add entry count badge

## Files involved
- apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/components/tree_selector.ex
- apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex
- apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/overlay.ex

## Verification
Run both TUIs in tmux side-by-side and compare /tree output:
- Node.js: ./bin/pi or npx @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent
- Elixir: ./bin/pi in this repo
title: opi-277: /tree command UI parity with Node.js
